t: SQLite: The Database at the Edge of the Network with Dr. Richard Hipp

q.x: (I highly recommend to watch it, if only to get a sense of the smart and funny energy that Dr Richard Hipp puts off!) [1]: [link]

desc: Dr. Richard Hipp—creator of SQLite—provides a great view into the history of SQLite and situations where it really shines. SQLite is a database designed to live at the edge of the network with no DBA to tend to it.

recs.stt: DuckDB – An embeddable SQL database like SQLite, but supports Postgres features
recs.x:
From the Carnegie Mellon DuckDB talk [3], I saw that you already have a zero-copy reader to the pandas memory data structures, so the vision I have is that DuckDB could be the universal SQL interface to arrow datasets which can then also be shared with more complex ML models. Is that something that we can hope for or are there obstacles to this?
